# Simultaneous Matchups & Initial Hygiene (`prep.R`) {#simultaneous}

```{r ch2-setup, include = FALSE}
source('R/00_setup.R')
```

To partition light attenuation among phytoplankton, non-algal particles, and dissolved organic carbon, we need field samples where **`chl_a`**, **`doc`**, and **`tss`** were collected on the **same day at the same station** (`MonitoringLocationIdentifier` and `date`)—which we refer to as *matchups*. Calibrating our bio-optical model additionally requires a same-day **Secchi disk depth (`secchi`)** measurement.

```{r build-simul, eval = FALSE}
am        <- get_aquamatch()                              # 490,209 joined 3-LAC records (1970–2025)
simul     <- build_simultaneous(am, require_secchi = TRUE)
no_secchi <- build_simultaneous(am, require_secchi = FALSE)
```

## Four Initial Hygiene Filters

Before statistical screening, `build_simultaneous()` in `R/prep.R` applies four simple, deterministic hygiene rules:

1. **Ambient water bodies only:** Excludes industrial/municipal `Facility` outflows, retaining `Estuary`, `Lake`, and `Stream` sites.
2. **True Secchi measurements** (for 4-variable calibration): Requires `sdd_approx == 0` (excluding turbidity tubes) and `sdd_mdl <= 1` (excluding $\le 0.01\text{ m}$ floor placeholders).
3. **Gross unit-error caps:** Removes obvious $1{,}000\times$ reporting-unit mixups ($\mu\text{g L}^{-1}$ reported as $\text{mg L}^{-1}$): $0 < z_{SD} < `r P$max_secchi_m`\text{ m}$, $\text{Chl }a < `r P$max_chl_ugL`\ \mu\text{g L}^{-1}$, $\text{TSS} < `r P$max_tss_mgL`\text{ mg L}^{-1}$, and $\text{DOC} < `r P$max_doc_mgL`\text{ mg L}^{-1}$.
4. **Same-day deduplication:** Collapses duplicate agency uploads of the same bottle sample (`distinct(SiteID, date, secchi, chl_a, doc, tss)`).

```{r simul-counts, echo = FALSE}
simul <- get_simul('simul'); no_secchi <- get_simul('no_secchi')
bind_rows(
  count(simul, type) %>% mutate(set = '4-Variable Training Matchups (Secchi + Chl a + DOC + TSS)'),
  count(no_secchi, type) %>% mutate(set = '3-Constituent Application Matchups (Chl a + DOC + TSS)')) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = n) %>%
  mutate(Total = Estuary + Lake + Stream) %>%
  select(set, Stream, Lake, Estuary, Total) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), fmt_n)) %>%
  kable(col.names = c('Matchup Dataset', 'Streams', 'Lakes', 'Estuaries', 'Total Matchups')) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c('condensed', 'striped'), full_width = TRUE)
```

::: {.decision}
**Why Streams Have Twice as Many 3-Constituent Matchups as 4-Variable Matchups**

Lake and estuary programs almost always lower a Secchi disk alongside water-chemistry bottles, whereas stream and river networks frequently sample chemistry (`Chl a + DOC + TSS/SSC`) without Secchi depth (`151,125` 4-variable vs. `311,057` 3-constituent stream matchups). Because constituent distributions are nearly identical with or without paired Secchi depth (`Figure 1a`), our calibrated regional model can partition light attenuation across all **`r fmt_n(nrow(get_final_data()))`** 3-constituent matchups without extrapolating beyond the calibration domain.
:::

## Spatial & Seasonal Footprint of Matchups

Across the conterminous U.S., **`r round(100 * mean(get_training()$long >= -90), 1)`%** of calibration matchups lie east of $-90^\circ\text{ W}$ and **`r round(100 * mean(get_training()$long < -90), 1)`%** (`r fmt_n(sum(get_training()$long < -90))` matchups across `r fmt_n(n_distinct(get_training()$SiteID[get_training()$long < -90]))` stations) lie in the western U.S.:

```{r simul-map, echo = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 4.6, fig.cap = 'Spatial distribution of simultaneous monitoring stations across the conterminous United States (a) and seasonal sampling distribution by month (b).'}
usa <- rnaturalearth::ne_states(country = 'United States of America', returnclass = 'sf') %>%
  filter(!name %in% c('Alaska', 'Hawaii'))
p_map <- simul %>% distinct(SiteID, lat, long, type) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords = c('long', 'lat'), crs = 4326) %>%
  ggplot() + geom_sf(data = usa, fill = 'grey96', colour = 'grey70', linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = type), size = 0.55, alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = TYPE_COLS, name = 'Water-body type') +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-125, -66), ylim = c(24, 50)) + theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = 'bottom') +
  ggtitle('(a) Monitoring Stations with Simultaneous Matchups')

p_mo <- simul %>%
  mutate(month = factor(format(date, '%b'), levels = month.abb)) %>%
  count(month, type) %>%
  ggplot(aes(month, n, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.78, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = TYPE_COLS) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()) +
  labs(x = 'Sampling Month', y = 'Matchups (n)', title = '(b) Seasonal Sampling Distribution')

p_map + p_mo + patchwork::plot_layout(widths = c(1.6, 1))
```

## Log-Log Covariance Structure

Log-log distributions across a 10% random subsample show the strong negative scaling between `secchi` and each constituent (`chl_a`, `tss`, `doc`), as well as the positive coupling between `chl_a` and bulk `tss`—which motivates subtracting living phytoplankton biomass from bulk TSS in Section \@ref(nap):

```{r pairs, echo = FALSE, fig.height = 6.2, cache = TRUE, fig.cap = 'Log-log bivariate scatter and density matrix across a 10% random sample of 4-variable matchups.'}
set.seed(1)
simul %>% slice_sample(prop = 0.1) %>%
  mutate(across(c(secchi, chl_a, tss, doc), log10)) %>%
  filter(if_all(c(secchi, chl_a, tss, doc), is.finite)) %>%
  GGally::ggpairs(columns = c('secchi', 'chl_a', 'tss', 'doc'), mapping = aes(colour = type),
                  lower = list(continuous = GGally::wrap('points', shape = 1, alpha = 0.25, size = 0.35)),
                  diag = list(continuous = GGally::wrap('densityDiag', alpha = 0.5))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = TYPE_COLS) + scale_fill_manual(values = TYPE_COLS) + theme_bw(base_size = 9)
```
